concept.name: Size-time priority
concept.definition: An order-matching priority in which size influences ranking among eligible orders and time breaks or contributes to the ranking, as used in specified non-displayed venue books.
concept.intuition: It describes the immediately available terms and ease of trading in an order-driven market.
concept.mechanics: After price and any participant tier are resolved, rank eligible resting orders using the venue's size-time rule; exact weighting or tie-breaking is venue-specific.
concept.failure_modes: Displayed quotes and depth can cancel, fragment across venues, or vanish under stress, so snapshots can overstate executable liquidity.
concept.misconceptions: A quote or narrow spread is not a guarantee that a large order can trade at that price without delay or impact.
concept.example: In a simple largest-first rule, a resting 1,000-share order ranks ahead of a 500-share order at the same eligible price, with arrival time breaking equal-size ties.
